newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin urges economic integration with Belarus.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin urges economic integration with Belarus.

text.p: Russia and Belarus, signing a union treaty on Wednesday, will concentrate on economic issues, especially revitalising ties between industries on a market basis, Russian President Boris Yeltsin said.

"The kernel of the Union is economy. We have to do everything to rebuild economic links between the two countries," Yeltsin said before the signing ceremony, praising Belarus's industry as a high-technology partner for Russia.
Yeltsin stressed the market nature of economic cooperation. Belarus has made little progress on privatisation and rolled back some other economic reforms under President Alexander Lukashenko.
"Co-operation on a market basis between Russian and Belarus enterprises will start, and Russia and Belarus will speed up their drive out of the economic crisis," he said.
Yeltsin said a currency union between Russia and Belarus was relatively far off.
"The union will give an impulse to unification of monetary-credit systems, but we still have to do a lot to introduce a single currency... there is no room for illusion here," Yeltsin said.
Economists say a monetary union could undermine the relatively stable Russian rouble and re-ignite inflation in Russia, if it is not handled carefully.
He said the union would not create a single state. Both members would retain their sovereignty, and the union budget would be used to finance joint economic programmes.
